- When sentiment turns sharply bullish (↑↑) or bearish (↓↓) in recent days, model tends to overreact — overshoots peak or troughs, especially in early 30d horizon.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model underestimates downside risk — forecasts too high or too low depending on direction.
- If sentiment is neutral or flat for 3+ days, model often fails to capture mean reversion — underestimates or overestimates continuation bias.
- In 30d horizon, model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements — especially after sentiment spikes or news events.
- When sentiment is bullish but news volume is low, model overestimates upside — fails to account for lack of momentum or market skepticism.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment changes direction mid-period — forecasts adjust too late or too aggressively.
- If sentiment is bullish and news volume is high, model often overestimates upside — fails to account for volatility or market saturation.
- In 30d horizon, model frequently underestimates final 3–5 days — especially if sentiment is bullish and news is rising — forecasts “flatten” too early.
- When sentiment is bearish and news volume is low, model underestimates downside — fails to account for hidden risk or market fatigue.
- Model often overcorrects after sharp sentiment reversals — forecasts swing too far in opposite direction of sentiment trend.
